original_question: Which human gene encodes DC-SIGN, the primary receptor that facilitates the entry of the West Nile virus into host cells?

final_qi.question: Which human gene encodes DC-SIGN, the primary receptor that facilitates the entry of the West Nile virus into host cells?
final_qi.long_answer: DC-SIGN (Dendritic Cell-Specific ICAM-3 Grabbing Non-integrin) is a C-type lectin receptor that enhances attachment and entry of several flaviviruses, including the West Nile virus, into dendritic cells. In humans, DC-SIGN is encoded by the CD209 gene located on chromosome 19p13.2–p13.3.

final_answer.long_answer: DC-SIGN (Dendritic Cell-Specific ICAM-3-Grabbing Non-integrin) is a C-type lectin receptor expressed on dendritic cells and macrophages that binds mannose-rich glycans on pathogens, including West Nile virus, to promote viral attachment and internalization. In humans, the DC-SIGN protein is encoded by the CD209 gene located on chromosome 19p13.2–p13.3.
